title: Rushing joins Moten; drummer Mac Washington
summary: Hinton sorts out the lineage; Jones describes Moten's drummer Mac Washington and his drop-in-the-bucket stumbles.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Just to keep the record straight so we can

make this sort of like a genealogy and bring it right down - it's so very interesting, you've got all so much of it here which is so perfect and beautiful... We're back with Jimmie Rushing and Bennie Moten... Now when Bennie Moten started his band you got Jimmie Rushing now singing -
Oh, no, he had already started; he was established.
I see, but now Jimmie Rushing is joining from Walter Page's band.
He joined from the Blue Devils. Then Basie came over.
Who played drums in that band, in the Bennie Moten band?

Mac Washington. Looked somewhat like Jimmie Crawford but very beautiful. What they used to call, they call bombs now, stumbles - he made stumbles. He made that connection from the interlude to the... - nobody could drop in the bucket like him. A lot of times they used to ask me to do recordings and I'd say, "Send for Crawford. I'm not going to play these 4 bars. I don't know how to play them yet. Send for Crawford to play these 4 bars and I'll finish the date... Because he knew how to play dum - de dum - de dum - drop it in the bucket. You know, that's Ask the man on the row.
